notes.title: Major Gameplay Update
notes.content: [p]We've focused this update on Gameplay systems. Making the experience richer, but also stranger.[/p][p]We are also going to release the first Narrative Update in 2-3 months, hopefully earlier, but these things take time. We'll be specifically working on new characters, new events, and most importantly we'll explore and delve into more detail regarding previous characters and some lore aspects.[/p][p]But for now - Here's what's new:[/p][p] [/p][h2]New Anomalies & Symptoms[/h2][h3]Shoggoth mimic (anomaly) [/h3][p]One patient..isn't what it seems[/p][h3]The Watchers (anomaly) [/h3][p]Something has taken interest in you.[/p][h3]More tool symptoms[/h3][p]New diseases for the Magnifier and Stethoscope to reveal. Eyes. Mouths. You'll experience it all.[/p][p][/p][h2]New Modes[/h2][h3]Infinity mode [/h3][p]Heal endlessly, rack up points.. Until you slip. Every death has a cost.[/p][h3]Do No Harm mode[/h3][p]Send even one patient at -1 or 0? The game ends. Be precise. Be mercilessly careful.[/p][h3]Time rush mode[/h3][p]Heal efficiently to earn bonus seconds. Fail, and your time bleeds away.[/p][p][/p][h2]Quality of Life Updates[/h2][h3]Skip tutorial [/h3][p]Unlocked after your first full playthrough. Get ready to test yourself. No handholding.[/p][h3]Magnifier UX overhaul  [/h3][p]Now you can look up/down using \[W] and \[S] keys. No detail escapes your attention.[/p][h3]Humor Circle UX[/h3][p]Drag with the mouse now [b][u]supported[/u][/b] - no more scroll-only frustrations.[/p][h3]Arachnophobia setting [/h3][p]No spiders. You're safe.[/p][p][/p][h2]Misc.[/h2][h3]New achievements [/h3][p]Endless mode now has new goals to push your limits.[/p][h3]Bug fixes & polish[/h3][p]We've addressed key bugs and improved overall performance for a smoother descent into madness.[/p][h3][/h3][h3][/h3]

notes.title: Changes to Book of Medicine
notes.content:
While the release date is getting closer, and there is a lot of work for us to be done, I'm changing the Book of Medicine to make it more clear and understandable. I have discussed it in our Discord channel, but wanted to share here as well.

These are four issues we have identified player's having trouble understanding:
[list]
[*] That the dosages do not stack
[*] That the medicine of the time and the game requires some Trial and Error
[*] That intervals in the Physical Symptoms book give a hint on what the answer can be, not that all three doses are the answer
[*] And finally on what to do when a patient has an allergy
[/list]

Here are the changes of the book, let me know what you think!

[h3]Four Humors and Medication page:[/h3]
"Remedies come in two categories. Precision medicine uses a distinct dose (1–9) for each humor—Blood, Phlegm, Yellow Bile, and Black Bile. Crucially these doses do not stack: a dose of “3” for Blood doesn’t combine with another “4” to make “7.” Each stands alone.

Alternative medicine simply indicates which humors (Vital or Digestive) need treatment and whether a Low (1–5) or High (6–9) dose is required, without pinpointing exact values."

[h3]Humor Wheel page:[/h3]
"In the uncertain art of healing, doctors sometimes resort to careful trial and error—especially when patients have no awareness of their ailments and offer no clues for a cure. Doctors find the best results by closely observing the effects of medications on their patients. The closer the dosage to the ideal, the better the outcome—finding the exact dosage always leads to Full Recovery, while the exact opposite results in Death. All other dosages influence the patient’s condition incrementally, based on how far they stray from the ideal treatment."

[h3]Physical Symptoms page:[/h3]
"Physical symptoms can appear anywhere on a patient’s body—sometimes requiring the patient to be undressed for a thorough examination. These signs narrow the possible dose to an interval, yet only one precise value within that range leads to Full Recovery. Remember that doses don’t stack. 

If no physical symptoms are present, administering Low (1–5) or High (6–9) medicine can still offer clues."

[h3]Allergies page:[/h3]
"If a patient is allergic to the humor and dosage that would cure them, the doctor must consult the Humor Wheel to find the closest safe dose. While it may not yield a Full Recovery, it avoids triggering an allergic reaction and still improves the patient’s condition."

I'll push these changes probably tomorrow - but I wanted to share it with you first!

notes.title: Do No Harm Demo Patch Note
notes.content:
Greetings, Doctors! We've been hard at work improving the Do No Harm demo based on player feedback. This update brings major improvements to lighting, sound, UI, localization, and several bug fixes. Read on for all the details!

[h2]Major Features & Improvements[/h2]
[list]
[*] New Allergy System: Overhauled how allergies are handled in-game, including new tutorial content and updates to the Book of Medicine.
[*] Opening Cutscene Changed: Removed the filters, and changed the presentation.
[*] Newspaper & Day Conclusion Updates: Conditions and text adjustments for a more polished experience.
[*] Several font issues resolved.
[*] New Character Portraits & Anomalies: More variety in patients and unsettling occurrences.
[/list]
[h2]Visual & UI Improvements[/h2]
[list]
[*] Lighting Overhaul: Improved lighting effects for a more atmospheric experience.
[*] Paper UI Updates: Enhanced readability and usability of in-game documents.
[*] Added a new page after diagnosing a digestive medicine symptom.
[*] Updated medical restrictions and allergy pages.
[*] Character Info Updates: Expanded details on patient allergies.
[*] Totem Animation Adjustments: Slowed down animation for better readability.
[*] Subtitle color and style updated for better visibility.
[*] Added a skip button for subtitle text.
[*] Adjustments to dialogue text scrolling for smoother interactions.
[/list]
[h2]Audio & Sound Enhancements[/h2]
[list]
[*] “Lights off” lamp oil sound.
[*] New sounds for Spider and other Insect creatures.
[*] Totem activation sound.
[*] Character Voice Changes: Dialogue voices removed, and replaced with a dialogue bubble sound.
[/list]
[h2]Gameplay & Bug Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Skips Now Work from Text: Improved skip functionality for dialogue sequences.
[*] Patients now correctly leave after finishing a conversation.
[*] Warning text added before anomaly days.
[*] Long totem texts now cut in half for better readability.
[*] Totem skippable event added.
[*] Single medicine cost added: 25 pounds.
[*] Laudanum: Purchase limit set to max 3 (10 pounds each).
[*] Splash medicine: Now functions as a main medicine but does not take a slot in the medical card.
[*] Second dose medicine effect visibility adjusted (0.5 effect displayed in the medical card).
[*] Selection of main medicines improved—if medicine is at 100%, no selection button appears.
[/list]
[h2] Miscellaneous Fixes & Adjustments[/h2]
[list]
[*] Monster Girl, Manipulator, and Cult Woman Event Updates: Adjustments to event timings and text.
[*] Book of Medicine Adjustments: Anomalies in the medical book removed.
[*] Additional Balancing Tweaks and general stability improvements.
[/list]
[h2]🩺 Coming Soon[/h2]
[list]
[*] Further refinements to patient interactions and medical treatments.
[*] More anomalies and supernatural events.
[*] Additional language support and localization improvements.
[/list]

Thank you for all your feedback and support! Your insights help make Do No Harm even better. Let us know if you experience any issues, and don’t forget to Wishlist on Steam to stay updated!

Happy diagnosing, Doctors!

notes.title: Daily Developer Diary for Do No Harm - Part 4
notes.content:
[h3]Looks like yesterday's post was a bit too long, so I’ll keep this one brief. [/h3]

We’ve completed the internal demo build and will be sharing it with the publishers we’re currently in discussions with. As for why we’re not sharing it with you just yet, there are still a few details to refine, and we want to run thorough internal tests first. The good news is that our initial testing didn’t uncover any game-breaking bugs, which is why we’re confident it’s ready for publishers.

We’re sharing the demo now because we aim to finalize our decision on a publisher (or potentially self-publishing) by the end of next week.

That's it for today. Tomorrow I'll be talking about the upcoming local festival we'll be participating in this Sunday. I'm thinking about cosplaying as a spooky doctor there 😅 😂
Although, I don't have the necessary get-up for the cosplay, so don't quote me on that idea.

notes.title: Daily Developer Diary for Do No Harm - Part 3
notes.content:
[h3]TL;DR[/h3]
[b]Manipulator Totem [/b]revamped: now rotates 3 times before locking out Laudanum. Spot [b]Anomalies[/b] using tools & books. Miss them? Lose [b]Sanity[/b] & face creepy hallucinations.

🕯 Keep the light on, treat patients right, and uncover the island's secrets to boost Sanity.
⚫ Stay in darkness, harm innocents, or help Cultists, and things will get... unsettling.

If your Sanity hits zero, an interesting (and creepy!) ending awaits.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Hello everyone! This one ended up a bit too long, due to some formatting experiment I'm doing.
As mentioned earlier, we’re introducing a new [b]Anomalies[/b] and [b]Sanity[/b] system, alongside changes to how the Manipulator Totem functions. Here’s what’s new and what to expect:

[h3]Manipulator Totem Revamp[/h3]
[list]
[*] Previously, the totem would simply rotate to warn you of the Manipulator’s visit and the hallucinations he sends.
[*] Now, the totem acts as a dynamic mechanism with three rotations, adding a layer of challenge.
[/list]Each patient now carries a small chance of bringing an Anomaly from the void. These anomalies vary in difficulty:
[list]
[*] Some will be [i]obvious[/i].
[*] Others will be [i]subtle[/i], keeping you in suspense (and maybe a little paranoid).
[*] Not every 'unconventionally' looking patient is going to be an Anomaly. Some are just born that way, you discriminating sicko!
[/list]To uncover the more elusive Anomalies, you’ll need to:
[olist]
[*] Stay vigilant, and look around the room.
[*] Use all available tools.
[*] Carefully consult the [i]Book of Medicine[/i] and check your [i]Work Table[/i].
[/olist]If you identify an Anomaly, [u]drinking Laudanum[/u] becomes crucial:
[list]
[*] You can now purchase up to 3 small bottles (replacing the single normal-sized bottle).
[*] Laudanum prevents the totem from rotating or can rotate it one step back.
[/list][b]Consequences of Missing Anomalies[/b]
If you fail to notice an Anomaly or choose not to drink Laudanum:
[list]
[*] [i]Your Sanity will decrease.[/i]
[*] The totem rotates forward one step.
[/list]If the totem completes [i]three rotations[/i], you’ll be locked out of Laudanum for the rest of the day. This will result in your Sanity deteriorating further, making the game progressively more challenging.

[h3]The Sanity System[/h3]
Sanity now plays a vital role in your gameplay experience:
[list]
[*] Low Sanity will increase hallucinations and amplify the void’s influence on both you and the villagers.
[*] The lower your Sanity, the more eerie and difficult the game becomes.
[/list]Should your Sanity reach zero, an interesting (but creepy!) ending awaits you.

[b]How to Manage Sanity[/b]
Here are some ways to restore or deplete your Sanity:

Increase Sanity:
[list]
[*] Use a source of light (keep it on as much as possible).
[*] Correctly treat patients.
[*] Progress toward uncovering the island’s mysteries.
[/list]Decrease Sanity:
[list]
[*] Stay in darkness or choose to not use the light sources.
[*] Harm innocent patients.
[*] Aid Cultists.
[*] Miss or ignore anomalies.
[/list]
We hope you enjoy these mechanics and the tension they bring to your journey. Stay sharp, stay sane, and keep the light burning! 🌙

Will you keep it together and Do No Harm? 👀 Let us know what you think! 
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

notes.title: Daily Developer Diary - Part 1
notes.content:
[h1]Daily Developer Diary for Do No Harm - Part 1[/h1]
This first update is a bit longer than usual as I’ll outline not only today’s progress but also the broader state of development. Starting tomorrow, updates will be much more concise.

We are currently focused on two main areas:
[h2]Demo and New Gameplay Trailer [/h2]

[b]For the Demo[/b], we came up with a new [i]Anomalies[/i] and [i]Sanity[/i] system that we are implementing. We believe it will give more purpose to the player, and intensify the atmosphere of the game. This system will immerse players in the role of a lonely doctor grappling with eerie horrors on an isolated island. While this enhancement extends the timeline for the demo’s completion, it adds meaningful purpose to gameplay.

In the meantime, we’ve introduced several quality-of-life improvements:
[list]
[*] New Tutorial: Covering the Humor Circle and Physical Symptoms mechanics.
[*] Pacing Adjustments: Tweaks to ease the steep difficulty spike between days 1 and 2, and make progression into later days more smooth.
[*] Extended Gameplay: Seven days of gameplay are now included.
[/list]
These updates will be shared with the community first, with public access planned for next week. The full demo is expected to be publicly available in about a month.


[h3]As for the New Gameplay Trailer[/h3]

The current trailer doesn’t effectively convey the story, so we’re creating a new one. To help achieve this, we’ve brought on an experienced Art Director from the film industry. Their insights will enhance the game’s visual quality and storytelling. Hopefully, I'll be able to showcase this difference soon.

The new trailer will focus on the doctor’s challenges in the village: managing an already difficult medical practice that becomes increasingly horrifying with the emergence of unexplainable creatures and diseases. The narrative will explore themes of resilience, sanity, and the struggle to uphold the principle of [i]Do No Harm[/i] in the face of unimaginable horrors.

Tomorrow, I’ll share details about specific improvements to the Stethoscope tool’s visuals.

Stay tuned, and thank you for being part of this journey! Love you guys for all of your support!
